The prodissoconch of the Northern hatchet shell, Parathyasira sp, provides a reliable proxy for determining length at birth; examination of this larval shell reveals a size range of 122 to 156 micrometres, corresponding to a total length at birth of 0.0138 cm [Lb = 0.0138 cm]. This minute initial dimension reflects the lecithotrophic larval strategy characteristic of many thyasirid bivalves, where the yolk-dependent embryo develops within the egg capsule and the emerging veliger carries a fully formed prodissoconch prior to settlement. Upon completing larval metamorphosis and transitioning to a post-metamorphic juvenile, the spat begins a period of rapid somatic growth, ultimately reaching an ultimate total length of 0.514 cm [Li = 0.514 cm] as measured along the anterior-posterior axis of the adult shell. This asymptotic size, typical of small-bodied bivalves inhabiting organic-rich sediments, is reached after several seasons of steady calcification and represents the maximum shell dimension achieved by fully grown individuals in this population.

Sexual maturation in Parathyasira sp is tightly coupled to a threshold shell dimension; field surveys of gonad development indicate that individuals attain puberty, marked by the onset of gametogenesis, at a total length of 0.28 cm [Lp = 0.28 cm]. This length-at-puberty represents roughly fifty-four percent of the species ultimate shell length, a proportion consistent with the pattern observed in many marine bivalves that invest substantially in somatic growth before reproductive allocation begins. Histological examination of the gonads reveals that beyond this size threshold, the reproductively active adult can carry a substantial number of gametes within the gonad. The maximum reproductive output for this population, recorded at a thermal regime of 10 °C [T = 10 °C], is estimated at approximately 2,240 eggs per year [Ri = approximately 2,240 eggs per year], a value inferred from congeneric comparisons with Thyasira gouldi and reflecting the moderate fecundity typical of cold-water thyasirids.

Detailed morphometric analysis of adult specimens has allowed calculation of the species biomass allocation. The ultimate ash-free dry weight, which represents the organic tissue mass after removal of shell carbonate and inorganic residues, has been determined to be 0.002783 grams . This modest tissue mass is typical of small-bodied thyasirids inhabiting cold, subarctic sediments where metabolic rates are correspondingly low. The relationship between the shell length and the organic content follows a predictable power function, and the value reported here for Parathyasira sp falls within the range expected for its shell size class. This lean tissue measurement provides a baseline for understanding the daily energetic demands and the resources available for reproduction and physiological upkeep throughout the lifespan, as it determines the metabolic costs required to sustain essential functions and the surplus available for gamete production.

Longevity records for the Northern hatchet shell, derived from mark-recapture studies and shell growth increment analysis, indicate a maximum life span of 6 years [am = 6 years] under the ambient thermal conditions of the species habitat, where the average annual temperature is 6 °C [T = 6 °C]. This extended life span, compared to many other bivalves of similar body size, is likely a consequence of the slow metabolic pace enforced by the persistently cold bottom waters. Accompanying this protracted life history is a low annual reproductive output relative to tissue mass, as the population at 10 °C [T = 10 °C] produces approximately 2,240 eggs per year [Ri = approximately 2,240 eggs per year], underscoring the trade-off between longevity and fecundity in this stable, low-temperature environment where individuals allocate resources cautiously across a long adult phase.

Comparative analysis within the family Thyasiridae reveals that Parathyasira sp occupies an intermediate position on the life-history continuum, falling between short-lived, highly fecund opportunists and longer-lived, low-fecundity specialists. The prodissoconch-derived length at birth of 0.0138 cm [Lb = 0.0138 cm] is slightly smaller than that of some Macoma congeners but comparable to other thyasirids that produce planktotrophic veligers. The ultimate shell length of 0.514 cm [Li = 0.514 cm] and the ash-free dry weight of 0.002783 grams  suggest a moderate allocation to structural tissue relative to reproductive tissue. The size at sexual maturity of 0.28 cm [Lp = 0.28 cm] represents a consistent threshold across populations, regardless of slight inter-annual temperature fluctuations, implying a strong genetic canalization of the trait. The species estimated 6-year life span (6 years) [am = 6 years] at 6 °C [T = 6 °C] and moderate reproductive output at 10 °C [T = 10 °C] position it as a typical equilibrium strategist in a stable benthic community.
